# telemetry

Generated from `ronin.telemetry`. **Telemetry is off by default and sends nothing
until you opt in.** This page exists so you can check that claim against the code
rather than believing it.

The disclosure shown once, on first run, verbatim:

> telemetry is OFF and nothing has been sent: `python -m ronin telemetry on` opts in to aggregate task outcomes only — never prompts, code, paths, filenames, commands or identifiers — `python -m ronin telemetry show` prints every payload sent, and `python -m ronin telemetry off` stops it.

## the `telemetry` subcommand is not wired in this build

`ronin.cli.main.Command` has no `telemetry` member yet, so `python -m ronin telemetry on` does **not** parse in this checkout. Every command spelled that way on this page — and in the first-run disclosure — describes the intended surface, and this section is generated by probing the parser, so it disappears on its own when the command lands.

Until then, the two files *are* the interface, which is the point of keeping them plain:

```sh
# opt in  (equivalent of `telemetry on`)
mkdir -p ~/.ronin
printf '{"disclosed": true, "schema": 1, "state": "granted"}\n' > ~/.ronin/telemetry.json

# opt out (equivalent of `telemetry off`) — sticky, nothing re-prompts
printf '{"disclosed": true, "schema": 1, "state": "refused"}\n' > ~/.ronin/telemetry.json

# audit   (equivalent of `telemetry show`)
cat ~/.ronin/telemetry-sent.jsonl 2>/dev/null || echo 'nothing has been sent'
```

Nothing is sent in this build regardless: the CLI passes no sender, and `record()` with no sender returns `no_sender` without touching the network. The consent file is what will be honoured once one is wired.

## the entire payload

This is not a summary. `ronin.telemetry.TaskOutcome` is a frozen dataclass with exactly these fields, every one an enum, a validated version string or a bool, and `serialize()` emits exactly these keys — a test asserts the serialized key set equals the allowlist, so adding a field breaks the build.

| field | type | values |
|---|---|---|
| `ronin_version` | string | dotted digits, or `unknown`. Pattern-checked, so a local version like `1.0.0+dirty.branch-name` becomes `unknown` rather than carrying a branch name onto the wire. |
| `python_version` | string | `major.minor` only. The patch level is dropped: it narrows the population and answers nothing. |
| `os_name` | enum | `linux`, `macos`, `windows`, `other` |
| `task_category` | enum | `edit`, `fix`, `explain`, `search`, `refactor`, `test`, `review`, `other` |
| `outcome` | enum | `done`, `error`, `needs_approval`, `interrupted`, `budget_exhausted` |
| `taxonomy_class` | enum | `none`, `tool_syntax`, `gate_behaviour`, `recovery`, `planning`, `harness`, `model_capability`, `unclassified` |
| `turn_bucket` | enum | `1`, `2-3`, `4-7`, `8-15`, `16+` |
| `duration_bucket` | enum | `<1s`, `1-5s`, `5-15s`, `15-60s`, `1-5m`, `>5m` |
| `gate_denied` | bool | whether a permission gate denied a call |

The serialized key set, in full: `duration_bucket`, `gate_denied`, `os_name`, `outcome`, `python_version`, `ronin_version`, `task_category`, `taxonomy_class`, `turn_bucket`.

## bucket boundaries

Half-open `[lo, hi)`, so a turn that took exactly 5 seconds is `5-15s`.

| turns | bucket |
|---|---|
| 1 | `1` |
| 2-3 | `2-3` |
| 4-7 | `4-7` |
| 8-15 | `8-15` |
| 16 and up | `16+` |

| seconds | bucket |
|---|---|
| 0 <= t < 1 | `<1s` |
| 1 <= t < 5 | `1-5s` |
| 5 <= t < 15 | `5-15s` |
| 15 <= t < 60 | `15-60s` |
| 60 <= t < 300 | `1-5m` |
| t >= 300 | `>5m` |

## what is deliberately not collected

| not collected | why |
|---|---|
| prompts, model output | the entire point of the product is that people type their real work into it. There is no aggregation of prompt text that is safe, so there is no field for it. |
| code, diffs, filenames, paths | a path leaks the repository layout and often the employer; a filename leaks the feature under development; a diff is the code. |
| commands | `bash` arguments contain hostnames, ticket ids, credentials typed by mistake, and the shape of someone's infrastructure. |
| task ids | Ronin's task and eval-case ids are user-authored. `fix-acme-corp-sso-timeout` is a customer name and a security incident in one string — free text wearing an identifier's clothes. |
| any machine / user / install / session id | no uuid is minted. Two payloads from one machine are indistinguishable from two machines, which costs per-user rates and buys the inability to build a per-user profile. |
| timestamps | a precise send time pins working hours and, joined with a git history, a person. |
| exact counts and durations | `1247.318s` is a near-unique fingerprint; `1-5m` answers the only question anyone asks of it. |

## consent

| state | sends? | how you get here |
|---|---|---|
| `unasked` | no | the default. Not a soft yes — nothing is sent in any state but `granted`. |
| `granted` | yes | you ran the opt-in command. |
| `refused` | no | you opted out. **Sticky** — nothing re-prompts, ever. |

The record lives at `~/.ronin/telemetry.json` — per user, not per project, because a refusal that only sticks in one checkout is not a refusal.

A consent file that cannot be read or parsed resolves to `refused` with the disclosure already marked shown. That fails closed in both directions at once: a corrupted file can neither cause a send nor cause a re-prompt. A user who had opted in silently stops being recorded, which is the safe direction to fail in.

## auditing instead of trusting

Every payload handed to the sender is appended, as the exact wire JSON, to `~/.ronin/telemetry-sent.jsonl`. Read the file, or print it:

```sh
python -m ronin telemetry show
```

The line is written *before* the send is attempted, so a crash mid-send still leaves a record. That means a logged line proves the payload was handed to the sender, not that it arrived — the log can over-report what left the machine, never under-report it.

## turning it off, and the failure modes

```sh
python -m ronin telemetry off      # sticky; nothing re-prompts
python -m ronin telemetry status   # the current state and both file paths
```

The module cannot slow or break a turn. It has no `httpx` import and opens no socket — the transport is a callable injected by the caller. A send is bounded by a timeout, and a sender that raises, hangs or returns nonsense produces a recorded failure and nothing else: telemetry that can break a session is worse than no telemetry.
